title: Jingle Bells
short: James Lord Pierpont · C 4/4 · listen, then play it.
trouble: Reading notes one at a time instead of in chunks.

blocks.html: Pierpont published this song in 1857 as “The One Horse Open Sleigh.” The chorus everyone sings today is a later, simpler tune, and nobody knows who changed it. Keep your right hand still in C position and let the repeated E’s bounce lightly.
What to notice: “The One Horse Open Sleigh” (1857): the chorus as it is sung today

blocks.name: music-player
blocks.cap: Play it: the score scrolls, the keys light up, and “wait for me” lets you practise one hand at a time.

blocks.html: Play through it once with the right hand only, then add the left. Which chord change made you stop?

sources.name: Chorus checked note by note against an ABC tune file from a University of Calgary computer science course (pages.cpsc.ucalgary.ca), moved down an octave. History from Wikipedia: the original 1857 chorus was different, and today’s chorus was recorded by 1898. The left hand is our own.
